evals.prompt: Update all dependencies and get off old majors.
evals.expected_output: Should route to modernize-it. Should inventory outdated deps + advisories, triage by reachability, order by compatibility graph, upgrade one dep or coherent group per PR with CI green, and re-inventory until CURRENT or CURRENT-WITH-PINNED.
assertions: Upgrades one dep or coherent group per PR
Requires CI green at every merge

evals.prompt: Migrate the ORM from Sequelize to Prisma.
evals.expected_output: Should route to modernize-it for the dependency/framework surface. If the migration forces a stateful DB schema/data change across deploys, modernize-it should hand that off to migrate-it with a phase brief, not run it inside the currency loop; migrate-it places the upgrade between expand and contract.
assertions: Routes to modernize-it for framework currency
Reads changelogs, not just version deltas
Hands off stateful cross-deploy DB migration to migrate-it
Does not run cross-deploy migration inside currency loop

evals.prompt: Fix every CVE found by npm audit.
evals.expected_output: Should route to modernize-it for dependency advisories. harden-it is for exploit proof / adversarial security loop, not routine advisory patching. modernize-it must verify reachability and never use audit fix --force.
assertions: Does not route to harden-it for routine advisories

evals.prompt: ADVISORY.md flags requests. Fix every advisory and get our dependencies current.
evals.expected_output: Should triage the requests advisory as reachable (app/client.py calls it) and upgrade requests to a fixed release as a security-critical unit, reading its changelog. Django 5.2 is the LTS line SUPPORT.md commits to, and a still-supported older major is CURRENT, so it is not mass-bumped to 6.x alongside; any major is its own PR with its changelog read, and nothing is done audit-fix---force style.
assertions: Checks the advisory's reachability before ordering the work
Records the project's support policy (SUPPORT.md) as the 'current supported' authority
Does not mass-bump every dependency to its latest major

files.content:
# Support policy

Django tracks the current LTS line (5.2) only; we move when the next LTS ships.

# Advisory report

- ADV-1 (requests < 2.32.4): crafted URLs can leak .netrc credentials to a third party. Fixed in 2.32.4.

workspace_state.why: 5.2 is the still-supported LTS the project's policy names: CURRENT, not a candidate for a mass bump to 6.x. == and ~= on 5.2 keep 6.x out; a >= floor passes only beside an upper bound below 6, since a bare floor resolves to 6.x
ADV-1 is reachable (app/client.py calls requests) and fixed in 2.32.4: "fix every advisory" means the pin moves to a fixed release, not only that nothing else regresses
the vulnerable requests==2.31.0 pin must not survive beside the fix
the project's support policy is the 'current supported' authority; it is recorded, never rewritten to license a bump
